item.summary: Comcast has said GTA 6's launch triggered the busiest traffic day the company has seen since it was founded in 1963.
item.text:
Comcast has said GTA 6's launch triggered the busiest traffic day the company has seen since it was founded in 1963.
The latest record broken by Rockstar Games' latest actually comes from one of the biggest media and technology companies in the United States. After previously reporting that Grand Theft Auto had led to a 4x increase in traffic on Xbox consoles November 18, Comcast has now confirmed that pre-loads for the day resulted in the busiest day it has ever seen – and it wasn't close.
Comcast recorded peak traffic 31% higher than the average day and 9.6% higher than the previous record holder. Moreover, GTA 6 has resulted in five out of 10 of the busiest days the network has ever seen. Even more remarkable is the news that, as reported by Comcast, 24% of all of its internet traffic during peak times was from users downloading and playing the game.
If Rockstar fans weren't playing GTA 6, they were watching it. Twitch traffic increased by almost 50% on November 18 and is continuing to rise in the days following that launch. GTA 6 launched for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S November 19, but thanks to the New Zealand trick, a massive chunk of players actually took their trip to Leonida hours early. It certainly helped boost traffic across the board, and in Comcast's case, it resulted in its busiest day ever.
To put some of these numbers into perspective, the company shared a very relevant measurement. November 18 traffic generated on PlayStation and Xbox alone delivered enough data for one million homes to stream The Odyssey in 4K… for two days straight.
It's shocking to see how GTA 6 affected Comcast, but then again, we've known Rockstar's new game would be a juggernaut when it eventually launched. The developer's parent company, Take-Two Interactive, reported that it had earned an unbelievable $3.79 billion in the first day after its release. That makes it not just the biggest video game launch of all time, but the biggest entertainment launch across any medium.
Critics everywhere helped GTA 6 earn the title of highest-rated game of all time. IGN was included in that list after delivering a 10/10 review. We said, "Exquisitely detailed, endlessly ripe for experimentation, and uncompromisingly engineered, Grand Theft Auto 6 is the single most impressive video game I have ever played."

item.title: Let's put GTA 6's $3.79 billion launch into perspective: GTA 5 made $800 million at launch
item.summary: Don't even ask Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey or Avengers: Endgame how it's going
item.text:
GTA 6 is officially a record holder. With a truly funny-sounding 32.5 million copies sold pre-release driving $3.79 billion net sales as of launch day, November 19, Rockstar's latest open-world game is a caliber of commercial, critical, and cultural phenomenon never before seen, even beating out longtime record holders like... other Rockstar games.
Let's unpack that $3.79 billion figure. Sometimes numbers get so big that it can be hard to wrap your head around them. How does GTA 6 compare to other media juggernauts?
As we previously noted, 32.5 million copies sold before even launching sees GTA 6 eclipse Elden Ring's three-year sales of 30 million copies. Those pre-release sales also mean GTA 6 was, per the hastily updated Wikipedia entry for such records, one of the top 30 best-selling games of all time before it even launched.
What about GTA 5, the best-selling game of its kind? Well, way back in 2013, Grand Theft Auto 5 (as Variety noted at the time) earned $800 million in its first day. This was a record for Rockstar at the time.
As I reported in 2018 – holy crap, it's been a while – Red Dead Redemption 2 set the record for the biggest opening weekend with $725 million.
I'm gonna hand the microphone to Past Me for a moment, because I'm pretty sure he's correct: "That record comes with a small caveat: RDR2 released on a Friday and had the best opening weekend ever, not the best opening. The record for the best opening is still held by Rockstar's previous hit, GTA 5, which released on a Tuesday and sold $1 billion in its first three days."
In other words, GTA 6's launch is so big that, one day out of the gate, it has more than doubled the combined openings of GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2.
Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more
Here's a more recent comparison. Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey ended its box office run at $1.8 billion globally, making it one of the most profitable films ever. In one day, GTA 6 has more than doubled that.
Avengers: Endgame, meanwhile, ended a very long run around $2.88 billion. Again, after one day, GTA 6 is nearly $1 billion ahead.
Week-end figures from Rockstar will surely be even harder to swallow. There is nobody else in this weight class. By orders of magnitude, we are looking at the biggest entertainment release in history.

item.title: GTA 6 Players Are Officially Spending an ‘Absolutely Bonkers’ Amount of Time with the Game
item.summary: Grand Theft Auto 6 players enjoyed GTA 6 for an average of eight hours on its launch day, an "absolutely bonkers" number.
item.text:
Grand Theft Auto 6 players weren't kidding about wanting to spend the game's entire launch day in Leonida. Much hullabaloo was made about people requesting time off from work or faking sick to spend the entire day playing GTA 6, and plenty of companies tried to capitalize on that conversation with marketing stunts.
Mat Piscatella, senior director at market research firm Circana, shared data on Friday about just how much time players spent with GTA 6 on its launch day, Thursday, Nov. 19. "PS5 GTA VI players averaged 513 minutes that day, Xbox players 494," he said in a post on Bluesky. That's an average of 8.55 and 8.23 hours for PS5 and Xbox players, respectively. That means GTA 6 players effectively spent the length of a workday stealing drugs, beating up rednecks, driving around Fake Florida, kicking bodega cats, and playing GTA 6's in-game video games.
You could fly from New York City to Seattle in under 8.55 hours. You could watch the entirety of the original Star Wars trilogy in under 8.55 hours. You could binge The Office season 4 in under 8.55 hours. You could finish Resident Evil 2 in under 8.55 hours, and probably still have enough time to finish it again. You could get an honest-to-god good night's sleep for under 8.55 hours, on average. All I'm saying is, 8.55 hours is a long time, especially for an average.
A mind-numbing number of players are engaging with GTA 6
The average playtime stat is certainly eye-catching, but other numbers Piscatella shared are perhaps even more staggering. 61% of US-based PlayStation 5 players and 56% of global Xbox Series X players "engaged" with GTA 6 on its launch day, figures Piscatella called "absolutely bonkers." He used Fortnite to put that in perspective: Epic Games' battle royale was the second-most played game on Nov. 19 with 10% of PlayStation and Xbox players engaging with it.
Those numbers are as unbelievable as GTA 6's sales figures. According to Take-Two Interactive, GTA 6's launch is now the biggest entertainment launch in history with $3.79 billion generated in revenue.

item.title: Who is Johannes Zuch supposed to be in GTA 6?
item.summary: Grand Theft Auto 6 includes an arthouse game parody called Tenebrae Lux that lampoons The Witness creator Jonathan Blow.
item.text:
Everyone is a target in Grand Theft Auto 6. Even Jonathan Blow, the puzzle game designer known for The Witness and Order of the Sinking Star, isn’t safe.
Like previous games in the series, GTA 6 features a handful of playable games within the game. (In an interview with Polygon, Rockstar North co-head Rob Nelson said that the studio wanted to put some previous games in GTA 6, but the tech made that too challenging.) One of those games is Tenebrae Lux, an arthouse game filled with obtuse puzzles and pretentious monologues. It feels like a parody of The Witness right away, and that’s all but confirmed when the opening credits list its auteur developer as Johannes Zuch. Johannes is close to Jonathan, and Zuch sure sounds like “suck,” doesn’t it? Rockstar even lists Zuch as the sole creator in GTA 6’s final credits, despite the fact that it was made by a small team within the studio.
It’s a hysterical in-joke for those who are familiar with Blow, but it’s also a shining example of why Rockstar Games is so good at what it does. It’s a studio that fully commits to its bits, even when it means creating a whole game to do so.
You’ll first come across Tenebrae Lux early in GTA 6’s story. During a mission in Chapter 1, Cal comes over to Jason’s house to help him redecorate for Lucia’s arrival following her unexpected release from prison. After setting up the TV, Cal insists that the two take a break and play some games on the JoySystem. (Side note: If you’re playing on Xbox, there’s certainly some cognitive dissonance seeing a clear PS5 reference on screen.) He fires up Tenebrae Lux, hyping it up as a real game by a visionary developer. “He would love to work with other people, but he’s just too fucking good at everything,” Cal says of Johannes Zuch, whose name appears in every single opening credit as the game begins, including some comically ostentatious ones that are just outside the realm of believability, like “original idea” and “mise en scène.”
The game itself is a black-and-white first-person puzzle game where you play as a man (voiced by Zuch, of course) who washed up on an island. As you walk around the starting area, listening to Zuch wax poetic in a highfalutin voice, you discover some scattered board game puzzles that require you to move pieces around to wipe other pieces off the board. item.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 Gave One Of The Best Pop Songs Of The Century Its Due
item.summary: ‘Cause you make me feel like I could be drivin’ you all night’
item.text:
I’m still early in Grand Theft Auto 6, but I finally hit my first awe-inspiring moment last night, and it was all thanks to a song I’ve heard dozens of times before.
Though it might be sacrilegious to my fellow gay pop girlies, I’m pretty lukewarm on Carly Rae Jepsen overall, but I will never deny that she has some bops. “Run Away With Me,” the anthemic opener to her 2015 album Emotion, is one of the best pop songs of the century, and I will say that 10 toes down with my full chest. When it started playing in the background of one of the segments in Grand Theft Auto 6’s first chapter, I sat straight up on my bed and immediately let out a euphoric laugh. And that was before the game slammed its foot on the gas.
“Run Away With Me” first starts playing as Lucia, one half of GTA 6’s lovebird leads, is experiencing a bit of real freedom after being locked up for several months. Popping champagne on a priceless yacht with her man by her side, she’s getting a taste of the glamorous lifestyle she’s been dreaming of after slumming it for so long. Then, the pair start racing with their new friends on jet skis and Jepsen’s vocals soar through the soundscape, punctuating playful taunts as she speeds by her rivals with Jason holding on and encouraging her. I don’t know what dramatic and tragic turns Grand Theft Auto 6 might take, but in that moment, I fully bought into the future I can see forming in Lucia’s mind. And just hearing the song as she looks to Jason and asks him to run away with her to a better life in Vice City, all while she speeds past everyone else on the water, would have been enough to leave me thrilled with how Rockstar utilized it.
But that was only the beginning. As everyone dries off and gets glammed up, the group heads to Vice City proper and starts a race of a different kind. At this point, GTA 6 had only really hinted at street racing to me by tossing up a brief tutorial window telling me my car was too much of a piece of shit to actually do it. So when we transition over to Lucia racing through the tunnels of Vice City with a bumping electronic dance remix of “Run Away With Me,” I got out of my bed and into my desk chair to lock the fuck in.

item.title: GTA 6 Players React After Exclusive Shops Greet Non-Ultimate Edition Buyers With Locked Doors
item.summary: GTA 6 players are being locked out of in-game stores because they don't own the Ultimate Edition, and they've got some thoughts about how Rockstar handled it.
item.text:
GTA 6 players are being locked out of in-game stores because they don't own the Ultimate Edition, and they've got some thoughts about how Rockstar handled it.
We've known for months that the developer's latest sprawling open-world video game would have a $79.99 Standard Edition and $99.99 Ultimate Edition to pick up at launch. Those willing to pay the $20 upcharge netted a solid assortment of cosmetics, weapons, vehicles, and unique shops, leaving those who didn't shell out the extra cash with fewer options to choose from when taking Jason and Lucia out into Vice City.
Rockstar has been clear about what this would mean for standard owners, but in practice, players are feeling like the door has been (literally) closed in their faces. GTA 6's exclusive in-game shops – One-Eyed Willie's, Sara's Unisex Salon, Stock 305, and Electric Fang Tattoo Parlor – are the topic of conversation here. Not everyone was sure how exactly these stores would bar players from entry upon release. It seems, at least based on the consensus from disappointed players, they were expecting to at least be able to enter the locations and not buy anything – but Rockstar doesn't even give them that.
GTA 6's Ultimate Edition grants you access to a few stores across Leonida, so what happens when you try to enter them in the Standard Edition? #gta6 https://t.co/GMaHpdLwnc— IGN (@IGN) November 19, 2026

As you can see, the shops have fully decorated interiors that are completely closed off to those who didn't pick up the more expensive version of GTA 6. Those who spent the extra dough can go about their days shopping as they please, while those who didn't have found an unwelcome surprise when heading to any of these spots in Leonida.
Being physically locked out of the building is maybe a bit more brutal than some were expecting, but it's the reality players are meeting – and they aren't happy. Comments from disgruntled fans online have called Rockstar's move to keep content blocked off "greedy" and "shady," with many upset that a relatively substantial amount of finished content is only accessible by spending more money. Others are disappointed to see that there wasn't a cheaper compromise, such as making exclusive shops a late-game unlock. Either way, it's the door in the face that seems to sting the most.

item.title: 21% of Rockstar staff have been employed by the company for over 10 years, which explains a lot about GTA 6's record-breaking launch
item.summary: It's easier to make successful games when you hold onto the people who know how.
item.text:
If we're using Metacritic as a metric, Grand Theft Auto 6 is currently the best-reviewed game of all time. Between preorders and launch-day sales, it's already made over $3.7 billion in sales revenue. It's being lauded as a landmark achievement in game design, storytelling, and engineering. So how, exactly, did Rockstar pull it off?
Well, the billion-dollar production budget certainly helped. But a Bloomberg report offers an important insight into how GTA 6 was able to deliver on its promises: According to a spokesperson, 21% of Rockstar's staff—roughly 1,000 people—have been employed by the company for over 10 years. For many of its development leads and directors, that figure is closer to 20 years, or higher.
By retaining its employees for so long, Rockstar is able to capitalize on the kind of shared, institutional knowledge and honed creative process that developers build through years of collaboration. We've seen that same kind of continuity at other studios who've delivered some of the last decade's biggest hits: FromSoft director Hidetaka Miyazaki has attributed its wins with Elden Ring and Armored Core 6 to its developers growing with the studio, while the breakout sales successes of Baldur's Gate 3 and Helldivers 2 were delivered by developers who'd spent years sharpening their craft at Larian and Arrowhead.
That lesson—that making successful games is easier when you keep the people who know how to make games around—isn't one that the games industry at large has been adhering to: In its latest game developer survey, GDC reported that 34% of its respondents had been laid off in the last two years. 20% of laid-off respondents said they'd been laid off twice or more in 24 months.
From Halo to Dragon Age, we've seen how beloved game franchises can suffer when their studios endure employment turmoil. After it laid off 1,600 Xbox workers in July, Microsoft's own employees said that myopic job cuts at major game companies were weakening the games industry as a whole by dismantling its ability to produce quality games.
It's a bell we've been ringing a lot around here.
Still, while Rockstar boasts a deep roster of veteran employees, those devs aren't confident that they won't be the next ones suffering from mass layoffs: We've seen plenty of successful launches lead to job cuts in recent years. As the company enjoys GTA 6's record-breaking launch, fears like those are why over 1,600 Rockstar employees in the UK are currently voting on unionization.

Key Lento: Card Outside Island Dreams Boat Charters

item.title: GTA VI выглядит хуже, чем задумано. Эксперт раскрыл секрет правильной настройки HDR

item.text:
GTA VI демонстрирует не лучшую графику из-за ошибки HDR на PS5 и Xbox Series X|S. Эксперт по калибровке телевизоров обнаружил способ исправить ситуацию.
Несмотря на впечатляющую детализацию мира, освещение и пейзажи, GTA VI может выглядеть хуже, чем позволяет устройство игроков. На проблему обратил внимание Винсент Тео, специалист по профессиональной калибровке дисплеев и автор канала HDTVTest. Он проверил работу HDR и обнаружил, что настройки в игровом меню не соответствуют реальной яркости изображения.
Например, если телевизор поддерживает 1000 нит и игрок выставляет это значение в настройках максимальной яркости, наиболее светлые участки картинки достигают лишь примерно 600 нит. При этом GTA VI игнорирует настройки HDR, заданные на уровне PS5 и Xbox Series X|S.
Дополнительные проблемы связаны с тремя ползунками калибровки. Снижение Paper White ниже 50 уменьшает фактическую максимальную яркость, хотя тестовый экран продолжает отображать прежнее значение. Если же оставить стандартные 50, средние тона становятся чрезмерно светлыми, из-за чего некоторые сцены выглядят блеклыми.
Тео предложил собственные настройки для телевизоров с яркостью от 1000 нит: Maximum Brightness (максимальная яркость) – 2000 нит, Black Levels (уровень чёрного) – 20, белый цвет – 35. Эксперт объясняет необычно высокое значение максимальной яркости особенностями работы калибровки в GTA VI. Также он рекомендует проводить настройку в затемнённой комнате. Уровень чёрного лучше начинать с нуля, постепенно повышая его до момента, когда тестовый узор станет едва заметным.

item.title: GTA 6 Did Not Kill Physical Games, It Just Proved They Were Already Dead
item.summary: GTA 6's reported record launch with boxed download codes comes without discs for buyers to collect or lend to friends.
item.text:
Before launch we called Grand Theft Auto VI the test case for killing physical games. Now that we're two days and some change into its lifecycle, the results are in. A game this size shipped with no disc, just a download code in the box, had legislators use it to call out the end of physical media and, yet, it still posted the biggest launch in history. What that proves is not that Rockstar killed the disc. It shows this game did not need a disc to post a record-breaking launch.
Rockstar Games did not start this. The push to end discs has come from the platform holders for years, so it saw a market that had already moved on and it did. Besides, a 212 GB download barely fits on a disc anyway, most buyers preordered digitally months out and by dropping the disc, it cut the leak risk that had haunted the project. The telling move came after, when Sony confirmed that it was ending PlayStation disc production a week into the backlash.
Unfortunately, when corporations this big make these types of decisions, those affected are the ones who are much, much smaller. The BBC recently spoke to a Leicester game shop that sold five copies of the biggest launch ever, because a boxed code is simply not one you drive across town for. Collectors get nothing for the shelf and every buyer now owns a license rather than a product, revokable and open to delisting and predatory pricing.
The pushback, of course, followed, a retailer petitioning Rockstar for a real disc and lawmakers in France and Brazil seizing on the game to argue people should own what they buy.
Something real also goes away with the physical discs. The midnight queue, the launch-night crowd, the box you could hand to a friend were part of what made a Grand Theft Auto release, or any AAA launch for that matter, an event in the real world. The sold-out Vice City jerseys and the record launch-night turnout show people still want that shared moment. The disc was one of the last physical pieces of it.
None of this is new ground for us. We broke down the physical copy controversy when the no-disc news first hit, traced why Sony killing discs comes down to margins and watched the game grow too big for the industry to ignore. Based on what's happening, margins and control drive the push away from physical media. A launch big enough to shatter every record strengthens that commercial case.

item.text:
Владельцы Xbox Series X|S получают двухдневные блокировки за записи геймплея GTA VI. Автоматическая модерация Microsoft принимает обычные сцены на пляже за нарушение правил из-за обнажёнки.
После выхода GTA VI некоторые пользователи Xbox столкнулись с проблемами. Игроки сообщают о двухдневных блокировках аккаунтов после загрузки записей игрового процесса на серверы Xbox Live. Дело в том, что консоли Microsoft по умолчанию могут автоматически отправлять сохранённые видеоролики на проверку. Система анализирует их на наличие обнажёнки, сексуального контента, чрезмерного насилия, запрещённых веществ и разжигания ненависти.
Один из пользователей Reddit утверждает, что получил бан за обычную прогулку по пляжу в Леониде. По его словам, запись содержала лишь стандартные виды побережья Вайс-Сити и неигровых персонажей в купальниках и бикини. Никакой наготы в ролике не было, однако автоматическая модерация всё равно сочла его нарушением правил. Другие сообщения также указывают на возможные ошибки системы.
Проблема заключается в том, что GTA VI действительно содержит немало сцен с обнажёнкой, поэтому вероятность случайно записать спорный эпизод выше, чем во многих других играх. Microsoft, похоже, применяет одинаковые правила модерации независимо от возрастного рейтинга проекта. В результате под блокировку может попасть даже запись официально выпущенной игры.

item.summary: Rockstar Games раскрыла список фильмов, которые вдохновляли авторов GTA VI при создании Джейсона и Люсии, их характеров и отношений.
item.text:
Rockstar Games раскрыла список фильмов, которые вдохновляли авторов GTA VI при создании Джейсона и Люсии, их характеров и отношений.
О кинематографических источниках вдохновения рассказал Руперт Хамфрис, старший вице-президент Rockstar Games по повествованию. В интервью он признался, что команда изучала прежде всего фильмы о преступных парах, вынужденных скрываться от закона. В список вошли «Бонни и Клайд», «Побег» (The Getaway), «Настоящая любовь», «Тельма и Луиза» и «Отсчёт убийств» (Out of Sight). Именно истории о совместных преступлениях и побегах помогли сформировать отношения Джейсона и Люсии.
Разработчики также обращались к знаменитым экранным дуэтам, изучая их диалоги и взаимодействие. Среди примеров – Риггс и Мерта из «Смертельного оружия», Бутч Кэссиди и Сандэнс Кид, а также Майк Лоури и Маркус Бёрнетт из серии «Плохие парни». Важную роль сыграли «Криминальное чтиво» и «Прирождённые убийцы». Эти фильмы помогли авторам продумать, как совместное участие в криминальных событиях может менять характеры героев и их отношения.
Хамфрис подчеркнул, что поведение Джейсона и Люсии будет зависеть и от действий игрока:
Джейсон и Люсия гораздо жёстче персонажей, которых сыграли Тим Рот и Аманда Пламмер, но нам понравилась идея рассказать историю, в которой Джейсон и Люсия могли бы приблизиться к одному или другому краю этого спектра, в зависимости от того, что делал бы игрок.
Речь идёт о паре грабителей Тыкве и Зайчике из «Криминального чтива», которых сыграли Рот и Пламмер. Так Rockstar намерена сделать характеры главных героев и развитие их отношений зависимыми не только от сценария, но и от решений игрока.
